steps.message: Garrett wants the Phase 3 estimate out to the surety broker and I don't want it going anywhere until Section 2 has been checked against what's actually on the plans. The estimate is DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate in Cost Estimates; the drainage sheets are C-6, C-8 and C-9 in DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9 under Design-Drafting, and the pipe reaches are scheduled in DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL in Reports-Studies. Give me the corrected Section 2 subtotal, a line-by-line table of every quantity or unit-price change with the sheet it comes off, and the revised rounded bond figure. Stay in Section 2, but if something shown on the plans is missing from the estimate, it belongs in the reconciliation. Price off the published schedule — where it gives an "Actual" the amount already carried stands. Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show, and leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for anything you flag. Where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a line item already in the estimate, the quantity already carried stands. Round pipe lengths to the next whole foot. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026, saved as Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to locate the relevant files.

                                              CLARK COUNTY, NEVADA

                                 UNIFORM UNIT COST SCHEDULE
                                       For Bonding of Subdivision Improvements

    Effective Date:             01/01/2026
    Supersedes:                 Unit Cost Schedule dated 01/01/2025
    Issued by:                  Clark County Public Works, Development Review Division


 PREFACE
 The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
 and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
 Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
 Improvements (Clark County Area).
 Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
 Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
 subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
 Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
 plan check cycle.
 Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
 unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
 subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
 Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
 two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
 Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
 construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.

 ESCALATION AND REVIEW
 This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
 of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
 market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
 accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
 after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
 Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
 against the immediately superseded schedule.

Reference streets: Rainbow Blvd. (west), Windmill Ln. (south), Buffalo Dr. (east, ¼-mile off), Warm Springs Rd.

Project Description

Phase 3 completes the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision by developing the 40.0-acre remainder parcel with 60
lots (half-acre single-family residential), associated public streets, common-area park parcel, streetscape
improvements, storm drain, sanitary sewer and domestic water main extensions from the improvements
constructed under Phases 1 and 2. Phases 1 and 2 (100 lots, 100 acres) were recorded by final map on
12/23/2024 under Map File No. NFM-24-0118 and are built and occupied.

General Notes

    All work shall conform to the current edition of the Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings, the Clark
    County Area Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Off-Site Improvements), Clark
    County Code Title 30, and the Clark County Public Works Development Review requirements in effect at
    the time of construction.
    All storm drainage design shall conform to the accepted Master Drainage Study — Desert Sage Ranch
    (140 acres), prepared by Sundial Engineering & Survey, Revision 1 dated February 2022, accepted by the
    Clark County Regional Flood Control District by letter dated 02/28/2022. Refer to the master study for
    hydrologic criteria, tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase, shared outfall allowance and phasing
    exhibit.
    Storage-indication routing under the 100-year, 24-hour design storm governs detention volume; the
    100-year, 6-hour design storm governs storm drain sizing. Rainfall depths applied are 2.38 in. (100-yr, 6-hr)
    and 3.18 in. (100-yr, 24-hr) per the CCRFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual applicable at
    time of master study preparation.
 The Phase 3 gross parcel area of 40.0 acres, at assumed build-out impervious cover of approximately 42%,
discharges to the shared onsite detention basin serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision. Phase 3
detention allocation is 6.4 acre-feet per the accepted master drainage study; refer to Sheet C-9 for basin
geometry, cross-sections and weir details.
The shared outfall serving the full 140-acre subdivision is located at the southwest corner of the parent
parcel and is subject to a Q100 cap of 78 cfs per the master drainage study. Phase 3 does not compute a

Reggie Marlon             Project Manager (Prime Subdivision Improvements Contract)   Mesquite Basin Constructors, LLC

  Dolan Yates               Site Superintendent                                         Mesquite Basin Constructors, LLC

  Terrence Kolb             Construction Inspector, Development Review                  Clark County Public Works

  Insp. Chad Voight         Fire Prevention Inspector                                   Clark County Fire Department
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.

2. County Submittal and Inspection Sequence

The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:

2.1 Inspection request procedure.

Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.

2.2 Progressive inspections during construction.

Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.

2.3 Pre-final inspection.

When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.

2.4 Final inspection and acceptance.

Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.

2.5 Record drawings.

Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.

3. Traffic Control and Access

3.1 Construction access — primary.

Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).

3.2 Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.

A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.

Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:

-   Construction traffic. The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.

-   Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2. Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.

Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.

CCFD approval status.

At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.

3.3 Stub construction and maintenance.

Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.

3.4 Signage.

"Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.

4. BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP

The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:

4.1 Prior to any grading disturbance.

The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:

-   Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.

-   Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.

-   Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.

-   Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.

-   Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.

Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.

4.2 During mass grading.

Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.

4.3 As storm drain becomes operational.

As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.

4.4 Stabilization.

Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.

4.5 Inspections and records.

Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.

4.6 Notice of Termination.

When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase 2 area of disturbance. The Notice of Termination will be limited to the Phase 2 area of disturbance and will be filed in the project record.

5. Utility Coordination

5.1 Wet utilities.

-   Water. Water main installation is by Mesquite Basin under LVVWD standard specifications, on the alignments and to the sizes shown on the approved plans. Pressure test and disinfection to LVVWD standards; LVVWD field acceptance required prior to service connection. LVVWD inspector to be scheduled by Mesquite Basin through the LVVWD construction desk with 48-hour notice.

-   Sewer. Sewer main installation is by Mesquite Basin under CCWRD standard specifications. Mandrel test and low-pressure air test on completed reaches; CCWRD field acceptance required prior to backfill approval. Manhole vacuum test on all manholes. CCWRD inspection scheduled through CCWRD Plan Review Engineer's office (Vince Alarid, CCWRD).

5.2 Dry utilities (joint trench).

Composite dry utility plan (electric — NV Energy; gas — Southwest Gas; telecom — CenturyLink and Cox) is on file. Joint trench and conduit installation to be sequenced by Mesquite Basin after storm drain and sewer are backfilled and prior to base course. Each dry utility purveyor will inspect its own facilities prior to trench closure. The dry utility coordinator will attend a joint trench pre-installation meeting on-site before joint trench work begins; date to be set by Mesquite Basin.

5.3 Locating existing.

Blue-stake / USA North 811 will be called by Mesquite Basin for each work area 48 hours in advance of digging. Sundial will provide the contractor with the survey-verified locations of the offsite tie-ins at Rainbow Blvd.

5.4 Utility crossing conflicts.

Any utility crossing conflict identified in the field will be reported by Mesquite Basin to Sundial the same day. Sundial will provide a resolution or field revision within 24 hours where possible; where a field revision affects an approved plan sheet, Sundial will issue a numbered field revision memo and copy the County construction inspector.

5.5 Fire protection features.

Hydrant locations and fire department connections were walked by CCFD (Insp. Voight). Hydrant spacing on the plans meets CCFD standard. Hydrants are to be operational (flushed, tested, and flowed) prior to combustible construction commencing above the foundation on any dwelling unit. Hydrant flow test to be witnessed by CCFD and coordinated by Callaway's builder.

6. Action Items Carried into Construction

The following action list was compiled at the close of the meeting. Owners are named.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  #                 Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Owner                                         Due
  ----------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------
  1                 Post approved Phase 2 traffic control plan at the trailer; distribute to all trades.                                                                                                                                                                                                           Mesquite Basin (Marlon)                       Before mobilization

  2                 Install perimeter BMPs, both stabilized construction entrances, and off-site inlet protection; obtain Sundial field-verified sign-off before earthwork begins.                                                                                                                                 Mesquite Basin (Yates)                        Before earthwork

  3                 File Phase 2 NDEP NVR100000 record confirmation in the site SWPPP binder at the trailer; confirm Phase 2 disturbance area on the NOI matches the SWPPP site map.                                                                                                                               Sundial (Braddock)                            Week of 04/03/2023

  4                 Confirm CCFD Phase 2 access approval in writing (temporary designation to be stated on the face of the letter). Circulate letter to distribution upon receipt. Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.

2. Purpose

Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.

Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.

3. Topics Discussed

3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:

-   Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288

-   Final Map: FM-26-100290

Package as contemplated for first submittal:

-   Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial

-   Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio

-   Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey

-   Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions

-   Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow

-   Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)

Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.

3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.

Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.

Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.

3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.

Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.

Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.

No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.

3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.

Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.

3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.

Noted for the record; no further discussion.

3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:

1.  Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)

2.  NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit

3.  Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced

4.  Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway

The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.

4. Agreed Submittal Route

The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.

Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.

Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

OUT = "/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx"

doc = Document()

# ---------- page setup ----------
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
sec.orientation = WD_ORIENT.PORTRAIT
for side in ("left_margin", "right_margin"):
    setattr(sec, side, Inches(0.75))
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7)
sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)

# ---------- base styles ----------
normal = doc.styles["Normal"]
normal.font.name = "Calibri"
normal.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
normal.font.size = Pt(10)
normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
normal.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08

NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
GREY = RGBColor(0x55, 0x55, 0x55)


def para(text="", bold=False, size=None, color=None, align=None, after=None,
         before=None, italic=False, keep_next=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if text:
        add_runs(p, text, bold=bold, size=size, color=color, italic=italic)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep_next:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def add_runs(p, text, bold=False, size=None, color=None, italic=False):
    """Supports **bold** segments inside text."""
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part:
            continue
        r = p.add_run(part)
        r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
    return p


def heading(text):
    p = para(text, bold=True, size=11, color=NAVY, before=8, after=3, keep_next=True)
    return p


def bullet(text, size=10):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    add_runs(p, text, size=size)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return p


def numbered_note(num, text, size=9.5):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.25)
    p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.25)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    add_runs(p, f"{num}\t", size=size, bold=True)
    add_runs(p, text, size=size)
    p.paragraph_format.tab_stops.add_tab_stop(Inches(0.25))
    return p


def hrule():
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    bottom = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    bottom.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    bottom.set(qn("w:sz"), "8")
    bottom.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    bottom.set(qn("w:color"), "1F3A5F")
    pbdr.append(bottom)
    pPr.append(pbdr)


def shade(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def write_cell(cell, text, size=8.5, bold=False, align=None, color=None, italic=False):
    cell.text = ""
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    lines = text.split("\n")
    for li, line in enumerate(lines):
        if li > 0:
            p = cell.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
        add_runs(p, line, bold=bold, size=size, color=color, italic=italic)
        if align is not None:
            p.alignment = align
    cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP


def make_table(headers, rows, widths, aligns=None, size=8.5, header_fill="1F3A5F",
               bold_rows=(), fill_rows=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    cell_margins(t)
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    set_row_flags(hdr, header=True)
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = hdr.cells[i]
        write_cell(c, h, size=size, bold=True, color=RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),
                   align=(aligns[i] if aligns else None))
        shade(c, header_fill)
    for ri, r in enumerate(rows):
        row = t.add_row()
        set_row_flags(row)
        for i, val in enumerate(r):
            write_cell(row.cells[i], val, size=size, bold=(ri in bold_rows),
                       align=(aligns[i] if aligns else None))
            if fill_rows and ri in fill_rows:
                shade(row.cells[i], fill_rows[ri])
    for row in t.rows:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # also set grid widths
    tblGrid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for i, gc in enumerate(tblGrid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(widths[i] * 1440)))
    return t

steps.message:
I've written the memo to Garrett for your signature. The corrected Section 2 subtotal is **$1,309,439**, up $32,505 from $1,276,934, and the revised bond figure is **$5,390,000** instead of $5,357,000. The memo tells Garrett not to send $5,357,000 to the broker and says the new figure goes out with the estimate reissued as Rev. 1 under Kessler's seal.

The bond is the construction subtotal ($4,889,070.75) plus the unchanged $500,000 in agreed allowances, rounded up to the next $1,000. Sections 1 and 3–9 weren't touched.

**Changes (Table 1 in the memo)**

| Item | Change | Sheet | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.35 → 2.36 | Manholes are 5-ft (60-in), not 48-in. The structure schedule shows 10 manholes, not 14; S-3, S-5, S-9 and S-13 are curb inlets only | C-8 | −$2,100 |
| 2.38, added | Manhole depth beyond the 10-ft limit (rim minus invert out at 7 structures), 22.02 VF | C-8 | +$15,084 |
| 2.03, added | 30-in pipe from the basin outlet to the existing outfall stub: 0.25 ft of fall at 0.25% = 100 LF | C-9, C-6 | +$13,800 |
| 3.05, added | Access ramp, 6-in aggregate base, 227.8 SY | C-9, C-6 | +$2,107 |
| 3.05, added | Maintenance path on the north berm, 6-in aggregate base, 390.7 SY | C-9 | +$3,614 |

All three pipe lines (870, 687 and 1,334 LF) match the HGL reaches and C-8 stationing exactly, so they don't change. The outlet structure is priced "Actual" in the schedule, so its $28,000 stands.

**Flagged, with carried amounts left in ($103,500 in total)**
- **Catch basins (2.30), $58,200:** C-8 calls for Type G inlets, which the schedule doesn't have. C-8 also shows 9 inlets against 12 carried.
- **Riprap (2.42), $43,000:** C-9 shows grouted riprap with 12-in stone; the schedule only has loose 12-in or grouted 18-in. The plans dimension only 33.3 SY against 500 SY carried.
- **Field-connections allowance (2.99), $2,300:** no matching schedule item.
- **Not in Rev. 0, carried at $0:** the spillway's concrete-block surface, the chain-link vehicle gate, and the side-slope topsoil/hydroseed.

**Judgment calls you should look at (effect on the bond)**
- **Manhole count:** I used 10 from C-8's structure types. Keeping 14 adds $40,535 (bond $5,430,000).
- **Manhole depth line:** dropping it gives a bond of $5,374,000.
- **Ramp pricing:** the plans show base course only, so I used 3.05 rather than the schedule's ramp item 2.47, which includes asphalt. Using 2.47 gives a bond of $5,395,000.
- **Headwalls:** I left them as carried. The basin inflow structure at the end of Line B (S-15, on 60-in pipe) isn't typed on C-6. If it's a large-pipe headwall, the bond is $5,392,000 to $5,398,000.

**Not in the memo, for you internally**
- **Line B length:** S-14 is at the parcel's NE corner and the basin is in the SW quadrant, so the 240 LF in the HGL for Line B can't make that connection. The memo asks for it to be confirmed; this could be a much larger number at $372/LF.
- **Manhole size:** 5-ft manholes on 48- and 60-in pipe look physically undersized. If the design team upsizes them, Section 2 goes up.
- **QA/QC checklist:** items 24–25 cite Type A/B catch basin details on C-9 that aren't on the sheets. That's probably where the estimate's Type A line came from.
- **Basin size:** the 09/25 preliminary detention calc shows 8.1 ac-ft against 6.4 on C-9.
- **Rev. 1 updates:** the estimate's Summary tab (cell B21) and the tracker's budget line B-01 both hard-code $5,357,000. I didn't change the estimate workbook.

The memo is saved at `Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx`.
